title: Fact sheet: polar wildlife and sea ice
subject: English
source: Written for english/y6 lesson 17 (Teacher's fact sheet: polar wildlife and sea ice (facts checked))
intro: Lesson 17. Use these checked facts as evidence in your letter about protecting polar wildlife.

panels.title: The Arctic (north)
points: An ocean, covered in sea ice and surrounded by land.
Home of polar bears, Arctic foxes, walruses and many seals.
There are no penguins in the Arctic.

panels.title: The Antarctic (south)
points: A continent covered by a huge sheet of ice, surrounded by the Southern Ocean.
Home of penguins, seals and whales; there are no polar bears.
The Antarctic Treaty (signed in 1959) keeps Antarctica for peace and science.

panels.title: Polar bears and sea ice
points: Polar bears hunt seals from the sea ice.
When the ice melts early in the year, bears have less time to hunt and must live on their fat.
They are strong swimmers, but long swims use a lot of energy.

panels.title: Emperor penguins
points: The largest penguins, over a metre tall.
They breed on sea ice in the Antarctic winter; the father keeps the egg warm on his feet.
If the sea ice breaks up too early, chicks can be lost.

panels.title: Sea ice is shrinking
points: Satellites have measured Arctic sea ice since 1979.
The area of ice left at the end of summer has become much smaller since then.
Scientists link this to the warming of the planet.

panels.title: What helps
points: Using less energy and wasting less.
Protected areas where animals are not disturbed.
Rules on fishing so krill and fish stay plentiful for penguins and seals.

panels.title: An Islamic reminder
panels.text: People are trustees (khalifah) of the earth: we look after what Allah has created and do not waste or spoil it.
